title: Best AI Chatbots for Microsoft Teams in 2026
summary: Explore the best AI chatbots for Microsoft Teams in 2026 to automate support, answer questions, and reduce ticket volume.
body_markdown:
Microsoft Teams has become the central nervous system for enterprise collaboration, with[over 320 million users](https://www.businessofapps.com/data/microsoft-teams-statistics/?ref=unthread.io) relying on it for communication and workflow management.


As organizations seek to automate repetitive tasks and improve response times, AI chatbots have evolved from simple FAQ tools into sophisticated agents capable of resolving support tickets, managing workflows, and executing multi-step processes without human intervention. The right AI chatbot transforms Microsoft Teams from a communication tool into an automated service delivery platform.


Whether organizations need to handle[employee support requests](https://unthread.io/solutions/employee-support?ref=unthread.io) , automate IT workflows, or route customer inquiries, this guide covers the 11 best options across five distinct use cases.


## **Key Takeaways**


- AI chatbots for Microsoft Teams now span multiple categories: native productivity assistants,[internal helpdesk solutions](https://unthread.io/solutions/it-service-desk?ref=unthread.io) , general-purpose coworkers, and customer support tools.
- Teams-native chatbots eliminate context-switching by keeping employees inside their primary collaboration platform while maintaining structured ticketing and SLA tracking.
- Top solutions like Unthread report[40% automatic ticket resolution](https://unthread.io/blog/ai-service-desk-tools) across IT, HR, and other internal support functions.
- Pricing ranges widely, from free tiers for SMBs to enterprise contracts with custom pricing.
- The best choice depends on use case: Unthread for internal support, Microsoft 365 Copilot for productivity, Viktor for cross-functional operations, or specialized tools for customer-facing chat.


## **Why Your Business Needs an AI Chatbot for Microsoft Teams**


The productivity case for AI chatbots in Teams centers on reducing context-switching and accelerating resolution times. Employees lose significant time daily switching between applications to find information or submit requests. A Teams-native chatbot eliminates this friction by meeting employees where they already work.


**Key benefits for internal support teams include:**


- **Reduced ticket volume:** AI deflection can resolve 40-80% of incoming requests without human intervention
- **Faster response times:** AI responds in seconds compared to extended wait times for human agents
- **24/7 availability:** Employees get immediate answers regardless of time zone or agent availability
- **Consistent service quality:** AI applies the same knowledge base and policies to every request
- **Scalability:** Handle growing ticket volume without proportionally increasing headcount


For[HR service desks](https://unthread.io/solutions/hr-service-desk?ref=unthread.io) , AI chatbots enable private ticketing for sensitive requests like payroll inquiries, parental leave questions, and benefits changes. Employees can submit these requests directly in Teams without navigating external portals, while the system maintains confidentiality through private channels or DMs.


IT teams benefit from automated handling of common requests like password resets, software access provisioning, and onboarding tasks. Finance, legal, and procurement teams can similarly automate approval workflows and policy questions.


## **1) Unthread**


**Best For:** IT, HR, and internal support teams managing employee requests in Slack and Microsoft Teams


Unthread is an AI-native internal help desk for teams managing employee support across Slack and Microsoft Teams. The platform turns any channel into a structured help desk with automated ticketing, routing, SLA tracking, and a purpose-built AI agent that resolves requests without human intervention.


### **Key Features:**


- 40% automatic ticket resolution validated across IT, HR, Legal, Procurement, and Finance teams
- Conversational ticketing that maintains natural chat flow while tracking everything as structured tickets
- [Self-learning knowledge base](https://unthread.io/products/knowledge-base?ref=unthread.io) that automatically generates documentation from resolved conversations
- [Workflow automations](https://unthread.io/products/automations?ref=unthread.io) using natural language, visual builders, or custom code
- Support for bring-your-own-LLM via MCP integration to prevent vendor lock-in


Organizations using Unthread report that the system automatically resolves about 40% of all tickets across different teams, saving countless hours for employees throughout the organization.


Unlike competitors that emphasize high deflection rates by mainly automating access requests, Unthread's AI automation spans multiple Tier 1 internal support workflows. The platform supports HR teams with private ticketing for sensitive requests like payroll, parental leave, and benefits questions, keeping everything inside the collaboration platform employees already use.


### **Pros:**


- Highest documented AI resolution rate among Teams-native helpdesks
- Easier admin setup and configuration compared to legacy ITSM tools
- Multi-channel support across Slack, Teams, email, and web portal
- SOC 2 Type II compliant with HIPAA BAA available


**Pricing:** Starting at[$50 per agent per month](https://unthread.io/pricing?ref=unthread.io) with a minimum of 5 seats


**Rating:**[4.9/5 on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/unthread/reviews?ref=unthread.io)


## **2) Microsoft 365 Copilot**


Microsoft 365 Copilot brings AI assistance directly into Teams, Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint. The tool excels at meeting summarization, email drafting, document analysis, and chat thread summarization within the Microsoft ecosystem.


### **Key Features:**


- Meeting transcription and summary generation within Teams
- Email drafting and response suggestions in Outlook
- Document analysis and content generation in Office apps
- Data visualization and formula assistance in Excel
- Grounded in Microsoft Graph data including emails, files, and calendar events


The strength of Copilot lies in its zero-setup deployment for existing M365 customers. Enterprise security features including SOC2 compliance and tenant boundary protection come built-in.


However, adoption remains limited. As of early 2024, Microsoft reported that its Copilot for Microsoft 365 had surpassed 15 million paid users. The tool focuses on individual productivity rather than team-level service management, making it complementary to rather than a replacement for dedicated helpdesk solutions.


### **Pros:**


- Native integration with all M365 applications
- Enterprise-grade security included
- No additional setup required for licensed users


### **Considerations**


- Limited to M365 ecosystem; cannot connect external tools
- Designed for productivity, not structured ticketing or SLA tracking
- Additional cost on top of existing M365 subscription


## **3) Viktor**


Viktor positions itself as a general-purpose AI coworker rather than a specialized helpdesk tool. The platform connects to thousands of external tools including Stripe, HubSpot, and GitHub with read/write access, enabling it to handle marketing, finance, operations, and engineering tasks from a single Teams message.


### **Key Features:**


- Code execution environment running on a persistent cloud computer
- Professional deliverable generation including PDFs, Excel reports, and web applications
- Persistent memory and skills system that learns company processes over time
- Proactive automation suggestions based on observed patterns


Viktor fills the gap between Microsoft Copilot's M365 focus and specialized IT/HR helpdesk tools. It handles tasks like pulling reports, updating CRM records, and generating analysis across multiple systems.


### **Pros:**


- Broad integration capabilities across business tools
- Free tier lowers barrier to entry
- Handles cross-functional work beyond support tickets


### **Considerations**


- Newer platform with limited market validation
- May be less structured than dedicated ticketing solutions
- May require more initial configuration for complex workflows


## **4) Moveworks**


Moveworks focuses exclusively on enterprise IT and HR automation, with pre-trained models for common workflows like password resets, account unlocks, software access provisioning, and PTO requests. ServiceNow announced its acquisition of Moveworks in April 2024, deepening its integration with enterprise ITSM infrastructure.


### **Key Features:**


- Pre-trained resolution logic for IT/HR workflows without custom development
- Multi-step task execution across identity management, HRIS, and ticketing systems
- FedRAMP authorization for government and regulated industries
- Native Microsoft Teams integration


Moveworks targets Fortune 500 companies with complex service management requirements and existing enterprise tool stacks.


### **Pros:**


- Mature enterprise solution with FedRAMP authorization
- Pre-trained on common IT/HR workflows
- Strong presence in enterprise market


### **Considerations**


- Enterprise-focused pricing may limit accessibility
- Requires significant infrastructure investment
- ServiceNow acquisition may affect roadmap independence


## **5) Social Intents**


Social Intents provides a GPT-4 powered chatbot that requires no coding to deploy. The platform trains on business content including PDFs, Word documents, Excel files, and knowledge base articles, then routes conversations to Teams channels when human handoff is needed.


### **Key Features:**


- No-code setup launching in minutes without developer resources
- Training on multiple content formats including documents and websites
- Live chat handoff to Teams agents when AI cannot resolve
- Multi-channel deployment across Teams, Slack, and website widgets


The platform serves SMBs seeking affordable automation without enterprise complexity. A 14-day free trial allows evaluation before commitment.


### **Pros:**


- True no-code deployment for non-technical teams
- Quick time-to-value for basic use cases
- Transparent pricing structure


### **Considerations**


- May offer less sophistication than enterprise solutions
- Primarily designed for external customer support
- Limited public validation through reviews


## **12) Aisera**


Aisera delivers agentic AI for IT, HR, facilities, and customer service within a single platform. The company was acquired by Automation Anywhere in November 2025, expanding its workflow automation capabilities.


### **Key Features:**


- Multi-domain automation spanning IT, HR, Finance
- 24/7 ticket deflection and auto-resolution
- Native integrations with Teams, Salesforce, Zendesk
- LLM Studio for custom prompt configuration


Aisera targets large enterprises needing comprehensive automation across multiple service domains. The platform competes in the enterprise IT/HR space.


### **Pros:**


- Broad coverage across multiple support domains
- Enterprise-grade customization options
- Strong workflow automation heritage


### **Considerations**


- Enterprise-focused pricing model
- Complex deployment requirements
- May be less focused than single-domain specialists


## **7) EzyConn**


EzyConn delivers a native Microsoft Teams app that resolves a significant portion of questions with AI before human agents see them. The platform installs directly from Microsoft AppSource and requires no webhook configuration.


### **Key Features:**


- Native Teams app with real threaded conversations
- AI resolution capabilities for common inquiries
- 5-minute setup with automatic knowledge base indexing
- Two-way agent replies pushing responses back to customers


The free tier includes 2 agents and 500 messages per month, making it accessible for evaluation. The platform focuses on customer-facing support rather than internal helpdesk use cases.


### **Pros:**


- True Teams-native architecture without webhook delays
- Free tier with no credit card required
- Fast setup time for basic deployments


### **Considerations**


- Newer platform with developing market presence
- Primarily for external customer support
- Integration depth may vary compared to enterprise solutions


## **8) Atomicwork**


Atomicwork delivers AI-first service management for IT and HR support directly within Microsoft Teams. The platform offers modern UX and workflow automation at more accessible pricing compared to enterprise alternatives.


### **Key Features:**


- AI agents for IT and HR support natively in Teams
- Ticketing, asset management, and change management
- Agentic workflow engine for service automation
- Native Teams integration included in base pricing


Atomicwork targets the gap between expensive enterprise tools and lightweight chatbots, providing structured service management with AI automation at mid-market pricing.


### **Pros:**


- AI-first design versus retrofitted legacy ITSM
- More affordable than top-tier enterprise options
- Modern interface and faster deployment


### **Considerations**


- Newer platform with developing market validation
- May offer fewer pre-built integrations than mature alternatives
- May be less suited for highly complex enterprise requirements


## **9) Glean**


Glean provides AI-powered enterprise search across Microsoft 365, Slack, Confluence, Salesforce, Jira, and dozens of other platforms. The Teams bot enables quick knowledge Q&A with citations showing source documents.


### **Key Features:**


- Unified search across all company tools in one interface
- Permission-aware results showing only authorized content
- Teams bot for quick knowledge queries
- Emerging agent capabilities moving from search to action


Glean suits organizations seeking to unify fragmented knowledge bases. The platform prioritizes search and retrieval over structured ticketing.


### **Pros:**


- Cross-platform knowledge search capabilities
- Permission-aware for enterprise security requirements
- Reduces time spent hunting for information


### **Considerations**


- Higher commitment levels may limit accessibility
- Primarily read-only versus action-taking
- Complements rather than substitutes for helpdesk solutions


## **10) Rezolve.ai**


Rezolve.ai offers an accessible price point among Teams IT/HR service desk tools. The platform handles password resets, account unlocks, software requests, and basic HR inquiries at a more accessible cost compared to enterprise alternatives.


### **Key Features:**


- IT service desk for common automation use cases
- HR service desk for PTO, benefits, and policy questions
- Native Microsoft Teams integration
- No-code workflow configuration


Rezolve.ai makes AI-assisted service management accessible to organizations seeking more budget-friendly options.


### **Pros:**


- Accessible pricing in the category
- Teams-first design approach
- Suitable for smaller organizations


### **Considerations**


- May offer different AI capabilities than premium alternatives
- Integration options may vary
- Developing public validation through reviews


## **11) Power Virtual Agents (Microsoft Copilot Studio)**


Power Virtual Agents, now part of Copilot Studio, provides Microsoft's official low-code platform for building custom chatbots. The tool offers visual flow builders, Power Automate integration, and multi-channel deployment.


### **Key Features:**


- Low-code visual design for custom bot logic
- Deep integration with Dynamics 365 and Power Platform
- Multi-channel deployment across Teams, web, and mobile
- Enterprise governance through Azure security controls
- Part of Microsoft's[AI services](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/ai-services/ai-bot-service?ref=unthread.io) investment


Power Virtual Agents suits organizations with developer resources who want to build custom conversational experiences within the Microsoft ecosystem.


### **Pros:**


- First-party Microsoft support and roadmap
- Integrates with existing Power Platform investments
- Enterprise governance built-in


### **Considerations**


- Requires technical resources to build and maintain
- More complex than plug-and-play solutions
- Custom development means longer time-to-value

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What is an AI chatbot for Microsoft Teams?**


An AI chatbot for Microsoft Teams is a software application that uses natural language processing and large language models to understand user requests, generate responses, and take actions within the Teams environment. These tools range from simple FAQ bots to sophisticated agents that can resolve support tickets, trigger workflows, and integrate with external systems.


### **How can an AI chatbot improve productivity in Microsoft Teams?**


AI chatbots reduce time spent on repetitive requests by automatically resolving common issues. Top solutions report deflection rates of 40-80%, meaning employees get immediate answers without waiting for human agents. This translates to faster resolution times and allows support staff to focus on complex issues requiring human judgment.


### **Can AI chatbots integrate with existing business tools like HRIS systems and ticketing platforms?**


Yes. Modern AI chatbots for Teams integrate with identity providers, HRIS platforms, CRMs, and ticketing systems. The depth of integration varies by platform. Enterprise solutions like Unthread offer native connections to dozens of tools, while simpler chatbots may rely on webhooks or middleware for basic integrations.


### **Are there free AI chatbot options available for Microsoft Teams?**


Several platforms offer free tiers. Viktor provides usage-based pricing with a free starting point. EzyConn offers a free plan with 2 agents and 500 messages per month. Microsoft 365 Copilot includes basic AI features in some M365 plans. However, free tiers typically limit functionality, resolution volume, or integration depth.


### **What security measures should I look for in a Teams AI chatbot?**


Prioritize platforms with SOC 2 Type II compliance, which validates security controls through independent audit. For healthcare and regulated industries, look for HIPAA compliance with Business Associate Agreements. Enterprise deployments should evaluate SSO integration, permission-aware responses, and data residency options. Platforms offering bring-your-own-LLM functionality provide additional control over data handling.
